ABOUT THE COMPANY
Mayfly Ventures Pty Ltd is a venture studio founded in 2022 and based in Melbourne, Victoria, specialising in building vertical SaaS and AI ventures. The team comprises engineers, designers, and venture builders who partner with industry experts to design, build, and launch disruptive technology products. Mayfly's core capabilities span venture building, solution design (UX/UI design, UX research, business process mapping, and product strategy), and full product development including MVP delivery, AI agent development, mobile applications, and SaaS platforms.

The studio works with both established businesses and growth-stage startups, specialising in rapidprototyping and iterative product development to help clients achieve product-market fit and reduce the technical barriers between idea and execution.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Mayfly Ventures is seeking an experienced Developer Programmer to join our team on a full-time basis. This is a hands-on, end-to-end product delivery role in which you will architect, design, build, and maintain web and mobile applications across concurrent client and in-house venture projects.
You will work closely with founders, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams to translate requirements into high-quality, scalable software solutions, leveraging modern no-code platforms, AI tooling, and best-practice software development methods.

KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
• Lead end-to-end design and development of web and mobile applications, managing priorities, timelines, and delivery across multiple concurrent projects
• Analyse user requirements and translate them into software specifications, user flows, information architecture, and technical design decisions
• Architect scalable, performant application structures including database design, backend workflow logic, and API integration strategies
• Design and develop responsive, high-fidelity user interfaces applying UI/UX design principles to maximise usability, engagement, and product quality
• Build and maintain integrations with third-party APIs and external services to extend
application functionality

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS
Candidates must demonstrate the following:
• Bachelor’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent
• Minimum 5 years of proven experience as a Developer Programmer, Software Developer, or equivalent, with a strong portfolio of delivered software projects
• Proficiency in no-code application development, particularly Bubble.io, with demonstrated ability to build complex, production-grade web and mobile applications
• Solid understanding of database design, data modelling, relational structures, and backend workflow logic
• Demonstrated experience integrating REST APIs and third-party services into production application environments
• Strong UI/UX design capability including wireframing, prototyping, and high-fidelity interface design using tools such as Figma
• Working knowledge of HTML and CSS for front-end customisation and interface optimisation
• Experience applying Agile methodologies and using project management tools such as ClickUp, Jira, Asana, or Trello
• Excellent analytical thinking and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail and system-level thinking
• Effective communication and stakeholder management abilities, with capacity to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced delivery environment

DESIRABLE ATTRIBUTES
• Experience designing and deploying AI-integrated product features and agentic or automated decision workflows
• Familiarity with additional platforms and tools such as Cursor, Bubble, Xano, and AI
• Experience with payment infrastructure integration (e.g. Stripe Connect) and end-to-end monetisation flow design
• Experience leading small development or design teams across concurrent client-facing delivery engagements
• Experience working across multiple industries including fintech, health, education, logistics, or hospitality technology sectors

HOW TO APPLY
Interested candidates should submit a current resume, a cover letter addressing the key
selection criteria, and examples of relevant projects or a portfolio link to careers@mayflyventures.com

About KRE8 IT
KRE8 IT is a Melbourne-based technology consulting company specialising in practical software delivery, low-code development, systems integration, and digital transformation. We work with clients to design, build, and support business-critical applications, with a strong focus on governed delivery, maintainable architecture, and high-quality outcomes.
We are seeking an OutSystems Developer / Consultant to support the design, development, implementation, and ongoing improvement of OutSystems applications for our clients.

About the role
The OutSystems Developer / Consultant will work across the full delivery lifecycle, including requirements analysis, solution design, application development, integration, testing, deployment support, and continuous improvement. The role requires strong hands-on OutSystems development capability as well as the ability to work in a consulting environment with clients and internal delivery teams.

Highly regarded

*   Relevant OutSystems certifications.

How to apply

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Build Australia's Next Generation Health Data Platform

Design the data that helps deliver better healthcare to millions of Australians.

Build technology that improves lives - Design and optimise enterprise-scale data platforms that directly support patient care, operational performance and nationally significant digital health initiatives.

Work at the forefront of AI and modern data engineering - Build cloud-native data pipelines powering advanced analytics, Machine Learning and Generative AI solutions using Azure, Microsoft Fabric and Databricks.

Shape the future of healthcare data - Influence enterprise architecture, governance and engineering standards across one of Australia's largest not-for-profit health systems.

What if your next engineering challenge could genuinely improve healthcare? 

Most Data Engineering roles focus on moving data from A to B.

This one helps transform how healthcare is delivered across Australia.

At St Vincent's Health Australia, we're building intelligent, secure and scalable data platforms that empower clinicians, operational leaders and researchers to make better decisions, faster. Every pipeline you build, every platform you optimise and every improvement you deliver contributes to better patient care and a stronger health system.

You'll join a collaborative Digital & Technology team driving enterprise-wide data capability across one of Australia's largest healthcare organisations. Working with Azure, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks and modern engineering practices, you'll help build scalable platforms that support advanced analytics, AI, automation and the next generation of digital healthcare.

If you're looking for a role where technical excellence meets meaningful purpose, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Program - Medicare Mental Health Check-In

This role supports one of Australia's most innovative digital health initiatives.

The Medicare Mental Health Check-In is a national virtual mental health service delivered in partnership with the Australian Government, providing accessible, evidence-based mental healthcare to people across Australia.

Data is fundamental to the success of this service.

As our Data Engineer, you'll help design and build the secure, scalable data platforms that enable real-time reporting, operational insights, advanced analytics and future AI capabilities that support clinicians and improve patient outcomes.

About St Vincent's Health Australia

For more than 165 years, St Vincent's Health Australia has been providing compassionate care to Australians.

Founded by the Sisters of Charity in 1857, we have grown into one of Australia's largest not-for-profit health and aged care providers.

Today, more than 30,000 employees deliver care across public hospitals, private hospitals, aged care, home care, virtual care, research and community services throughout New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland.

Our vision is simple but ambitious-to deliver excellent and compassionate care within a better and fairer health and aged care system.

Digital transformation is central to achieving that vision, and data is at the heart of everything we do.

The Opportunity 

This is far more than a traditional Data Engineering role.

You'll become a key contributor to the design, development and evolution of our enterprise data platform, enabling trusted data across operational reporting, predictive analytics, AI and enterprise decision-making.

Working closely with architects, analysts, clinicians, product teams and business stakeholders, you'll engineer modern cloud-based data solutions that are scalable, secure and built for the future.

You'll have the opportunity to influence engineering standards, contribute to enterprise architecture decisions and help shape the future of data across St Vincent's Health Australia.

This is a 12-month full-time fixed-term opportunity, based in our Melbourne Group Office with hybrid working arrangements.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll have the opportunity to:

Design, build and optimise enterprise-scale ETL and ELT pipelines

Develop modern cloud-native data solutions using Azure Data Factory, Microsoft Fabric and Databricks

Design and maintain scalable data warehouse and lakehouse environments

Apply software engineering best practices including CI-CD, automated testing, version control and Infrastructure as Code

Develop high-performing data models that support enterprise analytics and reporting

Build trusted data foundations that enable Machine Learning, advanced analytics and Generative AI initiatives

Develop vector database pipelines supporting Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions

Ensure data governance, security, quality and compliance within a healthcare environment

Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, architects and business stakeholders to deliver high-value solutions

Monitor, troubleshoot and continuously improve platform reliability, scalability and performance

Contribute to documentation, engineering standards and the ongoing uplift of enterprise data capability

About You

You're an experienced Data Engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges while delivering meaningful business outcomes.

You combine strong engineering capability with curiosity, collaboration and a passion for continuous improvement.

You're comfortable working across both technical and non-technical teams and enjoy building elegant, scalable solutions that make a real difference.

Essential

5+years experience in Data Engineering, Data Platform or Data Warehouse development

Strong experience with Azure technologies including Azure Data Factory, Databricks and Microsoft Fabric

Advanced SQL skills together with Python or Scala

Experience designing and implementing modern ETL and ELT pipelines

Strong understanding of dimensional modelling, relational databases and enterprise data architecture

Experience with Power BI, SSAS or comparable analytics platforms

Experience using Git, DevOps and CI-CD practices

Desirable

Experience working within healthcare or other regulated industries

Exposure to Machine Learning, MLOps or Generative AI technologies

Experience with Docker and Kubernetes

Knowledge of structured and unstructured data environments

Passion for emerging cloud and AI technologies

Why You'll Love Working Here

At St Vincent's you'll enjoy:

Building technology that directly improves healthcare outcomes

Working with modern Azure cloud technologies and enterprise-scale data platforms

Exposure to advanced analytics, Machine Learning and AI initiatives

Hybrid working arrangements that support flexibility

Competitive salary packaging benefits that increase your take-home pay

Ongoing professional development and learning opportunities

A collaborative, inclusive and supportive engineering culture

The opportunity to influence enterprise architecture and technology strategy

Working alongside talented professionals committed to in

Reofast supplies, fabricates and installs reinforcing steel for premium residential builders across Perth, taking projects from take-off and quotation through to fabrication, delivery and installation. We are seeking an experienced Construction Estimator to join our team in Perth, WA. In this role, you will be responsible for analysing structural and architectural drawings, preparing quantity take-offs and cost estimates, and developing reinforcement schedules and bar lists to support the accurate supply, fabrication and delivery of reinforcement steel products. This is a full-time ongoing position working 38 hours per week.


Main tasks:

-	Analysing structural and architectural drawings to determine reinforcement steel requirements for construction projects.
-	Preparing detailed quantity take-offs and cost estimates for steel supply, fabrication and delivery.

-	Preparing pricing breakdowns for materials, fabrication and logistics to support quotations and tender submissions.

-	Reviewing project variations and updating estimates, quantities and costs accordingly.

•	Ability to read, assess and interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications and construction contracts. 
•	Experience coordinating architects, engineers, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers, tradespeople and relevant authorities. 
•	Strong understanding of tendering, procurement, contract administration and project cost control. 
•	Ability to identify project risks, delays and budget variations and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
•	Excellent organisational, reporting and problem-solving abilities. 
•	Current Australian driver licence preferred. 
•	Relevant registration, licence or site accreditation may be required depending on the project and scope of work. 

Construction Project Manager Responsibilities

•	Plan, organise, direct, control and coordinate construction projects from commencement through to completion. 
•	Establish project plans, construction schedules, milestones, budgets and resource requirements. 
•	Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, technical specifications and contractual requirements. 
•	Determine appropriate construction methods, sequencing, labour requirements, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Coordinate the procurement and delivery of construction materials, equipment and services. 
•	Consult with architects, engineers, building professionals, consultants, tradespeople and technical workers. 
•	Negotiate and communicate with building owners, property developers, clients, suppliers and subcontractors. 
•	Prepare, review and contribute to tenders, quotations, contract bids and project proposals. 
•	Implement coordinated work programs across construction sites. 
•	Monitor project progress, expenditure, quality, safety, risk and compliance against approved plans and budgets. 
•	Ensure construction activities comply with relevant building legislation, Australian Standards, contractual requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Manage and monitor the performance, quality and progress of contractors and subcontractors. 
•	Arrange the submission of plans, permits and supporting documents to relevant authorities. 
•	Coordinate required inspections, approvals and project handover activities. 
•	Prepare progress reports, budget updates, risk assessments and project documentation. 
•	Identify potential delays, cost overruns, quality issues and construction risks and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Lead and supervise site managers, project engineers, supervisors, forepersons, subcontractors and tradespeople as required. 
•	Maintain effective communication with clients and key stakeholders throughout the construction process. 
•	Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, within budget and in accordance with the required quality standards. 

These responsibilities reflect the official ANZSCO functions for Construction Project Managers, including management of construction schedules, procurement, contractors, budgets, compliance, inspections and project resources.
